title: fix(supply): the admitted-set path has no 429 hop
description:
## .what

a filtered slug with no `floor` takes `getOneAdmittedSetCompletion`, which sends ONE request
with `allow_fallbacks: false` and no retry. a 429 from the host openrouter picked fails the ask.

the floor walk (`getOneFloorCompletion`) hops to the next qualified endpoint on a 429 or a 404,
so the two supply modes differ in resilience, and the slug gives no hint of that.

## .why it hurts

measured 2026-10-17 in rhachet-roles-bhrain CI: a live cache suite on
`openrouter/deepseek/flash/speed=min100tps&privacy=full` failed every ask of one shard with
`429 Provider returned error`. the same suite on the floor walk had hopped past throttles.

and the floor is not a substitute for a cache-sensitive caller: it ranks by sticker input
alone, so it lands on a cheap host that never caches (Makora/fp8, every round, cache read 0).
a caller who needs a warm prefix therefore has no supply mode that is both cache-sticky and
throttle-resilient.

## .the shape of the fix

1. in the admitted-set path, on a 429 (or 404), re-send with the throttled endpoint removed
   from `only`, honor `retry-after`, and report each hop in `attempts` as the floor walk does
2. refuse loud once the admitted set is empty, with the same funnel render
3. clamp: a test with a stub openai client that returns 429 for the first admitted endpoint;
   assert the second send excludes it and the reply is served
4. related, owed separately: rank the floor by cache-effective input cost (or offer a
   `cache=implicit` promise), so a cache-sensitive caller can keep the floor

## .found

rhachet-roles-bhrain @ beav/feat-review-cost-meter, release v0.41.0 publish run, 2026-10-17
